 Read more Read less I watch quite a lot of K-dramas, and apart from the storylines, characters and their wardrobes, one thing that often catches my attention is the way their homes are designed. While watching shows like Lovely Runner and 100 Days of Deception, I found myself drawn to the vintage-inspired furniture, warm wooden finishes, patterned walls and cosy little corners that make these spaces feel so inviting. There is something particularly charming about the classic furniture, wooden cabinets, decorative lamps and lived-in interiors that appear across several Korean dramas. 
 What I find even more interesting is how lighting changes the entire mood of these spaces. Even when the furniture, colour palette and decor elements look similar, the atmosphere can feel completely different depending on how a room is designed. Soft, warm lighting can make a living room feel cosy and nostalgic, while a strategically placed table lamp can turn an ordinary corner into a cosy reading nook. It is often these little details that make the interiors so memorable. From dark wooden furniture and patterned walls to warm lighting and vintage-inspired accessories, here are some ways to recreate that cosy, timeless K-drama-inspired look in your own space. 
 1. Bring in dark wood furniture for a rich, timeless look 
 One of the most noticeable elements in many Korean-inspired interiors is the use of wooden furniture. Dark walnut, teak, and mahogany-inspired finishes can give a room a more grounded, sophisticated appearance. Whether it is a wooden coffee table, a sideboard, a console, or a dining table, these pieces add visual depth without making the space feel overly decorated. If you already have light-coloured furniture, you do not necessarily need to replace it. Consider adding one or two darker wooden elements to create contrast. A walnut-finish bedside table , a wooden accent chair, or a console with a rich grain pattern can make a difference. For smaller spaces, choose furniture with a clean design and visible wood grain rather than bulky pieces. This helps maintain a sense of openness while bringing in the warmth associated with Korean-inspired interiors.
 2. Use warm lighting to create a cosy atmosphere 
 Lighting plays an important role in creating the aesthetics of a room. Rather than depending entirely on bright overhead lights, Korean-inspired interiors often use multiple light sources to create a softer and more intimate atmosphere. Table lamps, floor lamps and pendant lights can help achieve this layered effect. Look for lamps with fabric shades, frosted glass or sculptural bases that complement the rest of your furniture. For the living room, place a floor lamp beside an accent chair or a table lamp on a console. In the bedroom, bedside lamps with warm-toned bulbs can make the space feel more relaxing. Choose warm lighting for an elegant look.

 Plain walls are not the only way to achieve an elegant interior. Patterned wallpapers can introduce character and make a room feel more thoughtfully put together. Floral prints, delicate botanical motifs, geometric patterns and muted vintage-inspired designs are worth exploring. For an understated look, choose wallpapers in muted shades of beige, olive green, dusty pink, cream or brown. These colours work particularly well with dark wooden furniture and warm lighting. Plus, if you live in a rented apartment, you can prefer adding a stick-on wallpaper if you live in a rented apartment.
 4. Add vintage-inspired furniture and decorative details 
 Another way to recreate the look is by introducing furniture and accessories that have a vintage-inspired appearance. Think wooden cabinets, curved furniture edges, decorative mirrors, carved details and small display units. These elements can add a sense of personality to a room, particularly when paired with more contemporary furniture. A vintage-style console, for instance, can sit comfortably alongside a modern sofa, while a wooden display cabinet can be used to showcase ceramics, books and collectables. 
 Loading Suggestions... Loading Suggestions... Loading Suggestions... Loading Suggestions... 5. Layer your interiors with soft furnishings and textured fabrics 
 Soft furnishings are an easy way to introduce warmth and texture without making major changes to your home. Cushions, curtains, area rugs, throws and upholstered furniture can help bring together different elements of the room. Instead of choosing matching fabrics, experiment with a combination of textures. Linen curtains, cotton cushion covers, knitted throws and textured rugs can add visual interest while keeping the overall look comfortable. You can also introduce subtle patterns through cushions or rugs. Floral prints, checks, stripes and understated traditional motifs can complement dark wooden furniture and patterned walls. 
 Loading Suggestions... Loading Suggestions... Loading Suggestions... Loading Suggestions... 6. Display ceramics, books and decorative objects 
 Ceramic vases, handcrafted pottery, framed artwork, books, small sculptures and decorative bowls can be placed on coffee tables, consoles or open shelves. These objects add character while breaking up the visual weight of larger furniture pieces. Avoid overcrowding surfaces. Leaving some breathing room between objects helps each piece stand out and keeps the arrangement from looking cluttered. 
 Loading Suggestions... Loading Suggestions... Loading Suggestions... Loading Suggestions... 7. Bring in earthy colours to balance the darker elements 
 Dark wood and patterned walls can look particularly striking when balanced with a softer colour palette. Earthy shades such as cream, beige, warm brown, terracotta, muted green and dusty rose can help create a cohesive look. You do not have to use all these colours together. Start with a neutral base for larger elements such as walls, curtains and sofas, and introduce richer shades through cushions, lampshades, rugs and decorative accessories. 
 Loading Suggestions... Loading Suggestions... Loading Suggestions... Loading Suggestions... 8. Create a cosy reading or relaxation corner 
 Many on-screen interiors feature corners that look inviting enough to spend hours in. You can recreate a similar feeling by setting aside a small area for reading, relaxing or simply enjoying a cup of tea. A comfortable accent chair, a compact side table and a floor lamp can be enough to create this corner. If you have a window with natural light, consider placing the chair nearby and adding a cushion or a small throw. For apartments with limited space, a narrow bookshelf, a wall-mounted shelf or a compact wooden stool can serve as functional additions without taking up too much floor area. 
 How to recreate the K-drama decor aesthetic without overdoing it 
 Avoid matching everything : Mix contemporary furniture with vintage-inspired pieces instead of buying an entire furniture set. 
 Choose a consistent colour palette : Stick to a few complementary shades so that patterned walls, wooden furniture and textiles do not compete with each other. 
 Layer your lighting : Combine ceiling lights with floor lamps, table lamps and wall lights to create different moods. 
 Use patterns selectively: If you have patterned wallpaper, balance it with relatively simple furniture and understated furnishings. 
 Prioritise functionality: Choose furniture and decorative pieces that suit your everyday needs, particularly if you live in a compact apartment. 
 Give decorative objects room: Avoid filling every shelf and tabletop. More intentional home decor can make the interiors feel classier. 
 Frequently Asked Questions: What is K-drama-inspired home decor? K-drama-inspired home decor draws inspiration from the interiors featured in Korean television dramas. It often combines warm wooden furniture, ambient lighting, patterned walls, soft furnishings, vintage-inspired accents and mindfully styled decorative objects to create comfortable and visually appealing spaces. What colours are commonly used in Korean-inspired interiors? Warm neutrals such as beige, cream, brown and ivory are popular choices. These can be combined with earthy shades such as olive green, terracotta, dusty pink and muted mustard to add character. Can I recreate K-drama-inspired décor on a budget? Yes. You can add items such as patterned cushion covers, warm-toned lamps, ceramic vases, decorative trays and peel-and-stick wallpapers.
